g.text: read cart, owned addresses, address usage
[Each shop and available shipping method (UI requests in parallel)]
require owned address; shop in cart; supported method
require owned address and nonempty cart
require exactly one supported method per cart seller
collect selected items; merge product quantities
lock products in ascending ID order
[Inactive product/shop, insufficient stock, or invalid quantity]
snapshot product name, price and quantity
Checkout selects all cart items; reserve uses database locks.
The lower-level orchestration method has a fallback that inserts
quantity 2 of a first ACTIVE in-stock product if nothing is selected.
The customer checkout facade rejects an empty cart before this path.
